prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1148; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound in the left lane on a city street in Pasadena, Texas, when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 entered the roadway from a private drive and struck the front of Driver 1's vehicle in a low-speed head-on collision. Both vehicles sustained visible front-end damage. Driver 1 was seated in the driver's seat at the scene, and a Passenger was also in the vehicle; both the responding officer and a witness confirmed their presence. Driver 1 reported neck and back strain and was evaluated by emergency medical personnel. The injuries reported are consistent with the direction and force of the impact. Scene photographs confirm the general location of the vehicles and the front-end damage, though no independent witnesses to the collision itself were identified. Based on the available information, it is not clear whether all of the damage to Driver 1's vehicle resulted from this impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known to the reporting officer. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle. No citations were issued at the scene pending further review.
